title: Model artifact & audit chain-of-custody playbook
author: Arjun Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines an operational, auditable chain-of-custody (CoC) process for model artifacts (weights, tokenizers, compiled binaries, quantized blobs, and provenance manifests) and associated audit logs. It explains how to capture RBAC state, collect and package audit telemetry, preserve regionally constrained evidence, and hand off artifacts for legal/forensic review. The procedures apply to hosted, dedicated, and private deploys.

Scope
-----
- Incident types: suspected model exfiltration, unauthorized model modifications, data leakage via inference, and model-serving escalation requests from customers.
- Artifacts: model weights (.pt/.bin), tokenizer files, model config (json/yaml), KV cache snapshots, compiled runtime binaries, quantization metadata, provenance manifests, and request/response audit logs.
- Environments: Redwood-hosted, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem).

Key definitions
---------------
- Evidence bundle: timeboxed archive containing model artifact(s), audit log slice, RBAC snapshot, and an evidence manifest (see manifest example below).
- RBAC snapshot: a point-in-time export of entitlements, role bindings, service identities and active sessions relevant to the incident scope.
- Chain-of-custody stamp: signed metadata block appended to an evidence bundle describing collector, timestamp, checksum, location, and KMS key-id used for sealing.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Incident Lead (security oncall): overall approval and legal interface.
- Forensics Collector (SRE / Infra): executes collection commands, packages evidence, and uploads to evidence store.
- RBAC Owner (IAM team): verifies snapshots and provides supplemental entitlement logs.
- Custodian (Legal/Compliance): requests evidence retention extension and triggers formal legal hold.

Preconditions and constraints
----------------------------
1) Always confirm the incident classification with the Incident Lead before collecting artifacts that contain customer data. 2) Respect data residency requirements — evidence for a region-bound tenant must remain in that region’s evidence store unless legal has approved cross-border transfer. 3) When collecting private deploy artifacts, coordinate with the Private Deploys team and the customer contact for on-prem packaging procedures.

High-level process (summary)
---------------------------
1. Triage and scope: identify affected model(s), time range, and impacted tenants.
2. Snapshot RBAC and active sessions.
3. Extract audit log slice and correlated API/infra traces.
4. Freeze model-serving nodes (as needed) and export model artifacts and runtime caches.
5. Create evidence manifest, compute checksums, and sign (KMS).
6. Ingest bundle into regional evidence store with access controls and retention policy applied.
7. Notify Legal/Compliance and attach bundle to incident record.

Detailed runbook (step-by-step)
-------------------------------
1) Triage & Authorization
   - Incident Lead confirms evidence collection scope and legal constraints.
   - If customer tenant is regulated (HIPAA, GDPR), set confidentiality=restricted and route approval to Legal.

2) Capture RBAC state (mandatory before artifact collection)
   - Purpose: record who could access the model and which service accounts were active at T0.
   - Commands (examples):
     - Service identity list (kubernetes + internal IAM):
       curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://iam.redwood.internal/api/v1/roles | jq '.' > /tmp/rbac-snapshot-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json
     - Active sessions export (Auth service):
       rcli sessions export --since 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z --until 2025-01-01T03:00:00Z --out /tmp/sessions.json
   - Save RBAC snapshot to evidence staging area and record checksum (sha256).

3) Audit log extraction and correlation
   - Pull logs from the audit pipeline using log-store queries. Include request IDs, model IDs, and user/service identities.
   - Example KQL-like query (log-store):
     source:audit AND model_id:"model-abc" AND timestamp:[2025-01-01T00:00:00 TO 2025-01-01T03:00:00] | project timestamp, request_id, user_id, action, resource, outcome
   - Export logs in NDJSON; compute sha256 and include in manifest.

4) Model artifact preservation
   - If preservation will affect production SLAs, consult Incident Lead for canary freeze vs full node freeze.
   - Commands (examples):
     - Snapshot running container and copy model files:
       kubectl exec -n runtime svc/model-host-0 -- tar czf - /srv/models/model-abc | pv | gpg --encrypt --recipient "evidence@redwood" > /tmp/model-abc.tar.gz.gpg
     - Export KV cache (if applicable):
       redis-dump --host runtime-cache-0 --db 0 --keys "kv:cache:model-abc:*" > /tmp/kv-cache.json
   - Collect additional runtime metadata: GPU driver versions, runtime binary version, compilation flags, and quantization profile.

5) Evidence manifest (required)
   - A single top-level file named evidence-manifest.json describing all items in the bundle. Include these fields: id, collected_by, collection_time_utc, items:[{path, type, checksum, size_bytes, location, retention_policy_id}], rbacsnapshot_version, signed_by_kms_key.
   - Example manifest snippet (text example):
     {
       "id": "evidence-20250101-0001",
       "collected_by": "forensics-collector-1",
       "collection_time_utc": "2025-01-01T01:23:45Z",
       "items": [
         {"path":"model-abc.pt","type":"model-weights","checksum":"sha256:...","size_bytes":"123456789"},
         {"path":"audit-slice-20250101.ndjson","type":"audit-log-slice","checksum":"sha256:..."}
       ]
     }

6) Sealing, signing, and storage
   - Compute and record SHA256 checksums for each file.
   - Seal with KMS: use company evidence-seal key (kms://evidence/seal-key-prod). Example:
     aws kms encrypt --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/evidence-seal-key --plaintext fileb://evidence-manifest.json --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > evidence-manifest.json.enc
   - Attach a chain-of-custody stamp (signed blob) with collector id and certificate thumbprint.
   - Upload to the regional evidence store (S3 bucket or on-prem vault) and mark retention.

Retention and residency matrix
------------------------------
| Evidence type | Default retention | Regional constraint | Encryption | Owner |
|---------------|-------------------|---------------------|------------|-------|
| Model weights | 7 years (archival) | Must remain in tenant-region if tenant-regulated | AES-256 + KMS-seal | Security |
| Audit log slice | 10 years (per compliance) | Kept in region-bound audit-store; cross-border only via Legal | AES-256 | Observability |
| RBAC snapshot | 3 years | Internal only (no export) | AES-256 | IAM |
| KV cache snapshots | 90 days by default | Treated as PII if user data present; consult Privacy | AES-256 | Infra |

Access controls and proof-of-access
----------------------------------
- Only members of the approved forensics group may read sealed evidence buckets. Access is granted via timebound entitlement and JIT approval.
- Every access to evidence must generate an audit entry in the evidence-access ledger with fields: accessor_id, purpose, timestamp, justification, and link to incident id.

Forensics packaging checklist (must verify before handoff)
----------------------------------------------------------
1) RBAC snapshot present and checksumed.
2) Audit log slice in NDJSON and checksumed.
3) Model artifacts archived and sealed (GPG/KMS).
4) Evidence manifest created and KMS-signed.
5) Chain-of-custody stamp appended and logged in evidence ledger.
6) Evidence uploaded to regional store and retention policy attached.
7) Incident ticket updated with bundle location (internal id), legal hold flags, and custodian assigned.

Common queries and diagnostics (examples)
----------------------------------------
- Find requests that used model-abc with a high token count in the last 72 hours:
  SELECT timestamp, request_id, user_id, tokens_requested FROM audit WHERE model_id='model-abc' AND tokens_requested > 2000 AND timestamp > now() - interval '72 hours';
- Map role bindings for service accounts touching the runtime namespace:
  curl -sS https://iam.redwood.internal/api/v1/rolebindings?namespace=runtime | jq '.bindings[] | {role,subjects}'

Legal hold and retention extension process
------------------------------------------
- Custodian (Legal) files a retention extension request in the incident ticket. Include reason, extended retention window, and affected bundles.
- Security approves if the extension is consistent with internal policy and regional law.
- For cross-border transfer requests, Legal must complete a Data Transfer Impact Assessment and obtain Exec approval.

Post-collection: verification and cleanup
----------------------------------------
- Within 72 hours, the RBAC Owner must validate the snapshot for completeness and sign the verification record.
- If nodes were frozen for collection, SRE must implement scheduled rollout or rollback plan to resume normal service with minimal downtime (documented steps and release owner).

Appendices
---------
A. Evidence manifest fields (reference)
- id, version, collected_by, collection_time_utc, items[], retention_policy_id, sealed_by_kms_key, chain_of_custody_stamp

B. Example minimal evidence manifest (text)
- See step 5 example above; include full JSON file in the incident ticket when uploading.

C. Related runbooks and pages
- Incident evidence orchestration for multi-tenant model failures (link in related_pages).
- Audit schema contract and retention runbook.

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary: security-oncall@redwood.ai (pager)
- Forensics lead: Marek Novak (pager)
- IAM escalation: iam-ops@redwood.ai

Notes and rationale
-------------------
This playbook centralizes model-specific forensic handling because model artifacts present unique provenance requirements (weights can be forked, quantized artifacts change signatures). We treat model weights and audit slices as first-class evidence and apply stricter retention and sealing than generic logs to maintain legal defensibility.
